questions.question_text: Which unit is more suitable for recording the area of a suburban park covering about $80\,000\text{ m}^{2}$?

options.why: Chose a region-sized unit that is too large for a suburban park.
Used a unit of length rather than a square unit for area.
Used a cubic unit for volume instead of a unit for land area.

questions.solution_text:
$80\,000\text{ m}^2=8\text{ ha}$.
Hectares give the more suitable-sized measure for this park.

options.why: Divided by $1\,000$ instead of by $10\,000$ square metres per hectare.
Divided by $100$ instead of by $10\,000$ square metres per hectare.
Multiplied by $10$ instead of dividing by $10\,000$ to change to a larger unit.
Multiplied by $1\,000$ instead of by $10\,000$ square metres per hectare.
Multiplied by $100$ instead of by $10\,000$ square metres per hectare.
Divided by $10\,000$ even though converting from hectares to the smaller square-metre unit requires multiplication.

questions.question_text: A reserve covers $3.6$ square kilometres. Which correctly records this area using a unit symbol?

options.why: Used a length unit rather than square kilometres for area.
Used a volume unit rather than square kilometres for area.
Changed the stated unit from square kilometres to hectares without justification.

questions.solution_text:
The unit symbol for square kilometres is km$^2$.
$3.6\text{ km}^2$

questions.question_text: Which area is larger: $95$ ha or $1\,100\,000\text{ m}^2$?

options.why: Reversed the comparison after changing the square metres to $110$ ha.
Treated $1\,100\,000\text{ m}^2$ as $950\,000\text{ m}^2$, which would equal $95$ ha.
Missed that $10\,000\text{ m}^2=1$ ha allows both areas to be recorded in hectares.

questions.question_text:
A reserve joins parcels of $850\,000\text{ m}^2$ and $40$ ha.
What is the total area in hectares?

options.why: Divided $850\,000$ by $1\,000\,000$ instead of $10\,000$, then added the resulting $0.85$ to $40$.
Divided $850\,000$ by $100\,000$ instead of $10\,000$, then added the resulting $8.5$ to $40$.
Treated $40$ ha as $4\,000$ ha before adding the correctly converted $85$ ha.
